question: Following the postponement of the decision to re-authorise Brazilian poultry and honey for the European Union market, serious questions are being raised about the effectiveness of Brazil’s system for monitoring the use of antimicrobials. The Commission, despite its earlier reservations regarding the system of controls, has put forward a proposal to resume the export of these products. At the same time, some Member States have highlighted the need for further clarifications and guarantees. In this connection: 1.

What specific findings from the audit carried out in Brazil justify the proposal to resume the placing of poultry and honey onto the Union market, and will the Commission publish the full results of the audit, together with information on the irregularities identified and the corrective measures taken?

How does the Commission intend to ensure that products imported from Brazil comply with EU requirements on the use of antimicrobials? Does it envisage additional checks on farms, feed, production facilities and supply chains, and will it commit to not resuming imports until all the concerns raised have been independently assessed?

What have been the effects of the EU–Mercosur Agreement on the European agri-food sector to date, and does the Commission have data to hand on changes in import volumes, prices and the situation of producers in individual Member States, including Poland?
